fields.name: itemCode
fields.label: Item Code
fields.sourceQuote: Record the Item Code values. You will use this exact reference when importing your vendor access values by their Vendor Code value.

Two hard constraints from elsewhere: (1) exact-match on import - 'The code format (EAST; NORTH) for each list item must be typed exactly as you have entered them here in your import.' (same file); (2) when an expense type is the first connected-list field, the Item Code must match the expense type code - 'with an Item Code that _exactly_ matches that of the expense type you are using (example: Awards = "AWRDS")' (use-an-expense-type-as-the-first-field-in-a-connected-list-e0c5f415.md). No length or character-set rule is documented. The Processor-side Query Builder can search list items by this code (Display List Code check box, search-queries-by-list-item-code-08d2dba9.md) - that check box is a Query Builder control, NOT a List Management control, so it is not emitted here. FOLDED FORWARD from the dropped duplicate 'listItemCode' (tables lens): downstream import specs constrain this code to a maximum of 32 characters (the-import-template-fields-and-descriptions-8b4aa547.md; import-settings-record-type-200-format-c244e3ab.md) - but BOTH state that about the IMPORT COLUMN, not about the List Management entry field, so it is recorded as a downstream dependency and NOT as a validated limit on this control. The consuming rule from import-allocations-5ca442db.md is 'It is critical that import values be the list item code, and not the list item name (the display name) value.'

verifyNotes: REFUTER PAGE-LEVEL FINDINGS AND WHAT I DID ABOUT THEM. (1) GROUNDING: refuter-1 grep-verified all 25 distinct quote strings across the three extraction files and found zero quote defects (verbatimVariantIndex 0 everywhere; every variantSpellings array had exactly one entry). I re-ran grep -F -c independently on all 30 lens records, including every twin I did not emit: ALL returned 1. Every record in this roster was pulled programmatically out of the extraction JSON - no sourceQuote was retyped. No quote was hand-authored, so no new grounding risk was introduced. (2) RAW TABLES: grep -c '<table' on all four cited files (cc91aa73, f3fc8bee, 1eaafd29, e0c5f415) returns 0, so fromRawHtmlTable:false is correct on all 14 records and no false flag needed clearing. There is no page-relevant raw <table> file for List Management in either guide directory. (3) THE ONE TRUE REPAIR: newListCategoryOption carried fieldType 'radio' (procedures lens) vs 'dropdown' (crosscut lens), with the corpus supporting neither - the only sentence is 'Create New: Select New List Category and, in Add New List Category, type a name and select Save.' Repaired to 'unknown', and the underlying ambiguity (is New List Category a standalone control or an option value inside listCategory?) is RECORDED AS UNDETERMINED rather than resolved, with an explicit instruction that if it is ever established to be a value it must move into listCategory.validValues and this field must be removed, so the string is never counted twice. (4) THE INVENTED-VALUE CATCH: the tables lens's dropped twin listCategorySelector carried validValues ['New List Category'] plus a matching valueSetCandidate. I did NOT carry either forward. The corpus never states that the New List Category entry lives inside the category control; membership is plausible but unstated, which is exactly the completion class this project has already had to delete twice. RECOMMENDATION TO THE MERGER: DROP that value set outright rather than rewiring its appliesToField to listCategory - rewiring re-asserts the unproven membership. Every one of the 14 surviving records has validValues []. 'Allocations' (illustrative existing category), EAST/NORTH and the four Divisions (the guide's worked example), and AWRDS were all correctly kept out of validValues by all three lenses; I confirm those exclusions - they are tenant or example data, not documented system enumerations. (5) REFUTER DISAGREEMENTS I HAD TO SETTLE (both are duplicate pairs where each refuter kept the opposite twin, so both names arrived in the REPAIR bucket). newButton vs newListButton: kept newListButton, because field.exceptions.newButton already means a different control in the existing graph and this page carries a second New (listItemsNewButton) that the bare name does not disambiguate against. multiLevelSubLevel vs addSubLevels: kept addSubLevels, because it already carries the two findings refuter-1 asked to be folded forward (no documented depth limit on List Management; depth bounded only downstream by the compressed range Level 1 Code - Level 10 Code). Both losers are logged in dropped[] with duplicateOf. This is why 16 inputs yield 14 records: the two removals are intra-page duplicates of surviving controls, not lost surface. (6) FOLD-FORWARDS the refuters ordered before discarding duplicates, all done: listItemCode's 32-character import-column limit (with the caveat preserved that it is stated about the IMPORT COLUMN, not this entry field) and the import-allocations rule 'It is critical that import values be the list item code, and not the list item name (the display name) value.' into itemCode; listItemName's UNDETERMINED note into itemName; listCategorySelector's value-set warning into listCategory. I grep-verified the import-allocations sentence (present in admin-guides/import-allocations-5ca442db.md) before quoting it in a note. (7) VARIANT SELECTION: where a control was found by two lenses with different but equally verbatim quotes, I took the record whose notes carry more documented constraint, and for itemName I took refuter-1's explicit recommendation - the crosscut's full-sentence quote, so the conditional 'If the name is to appear the same for connected list audit rules' survives inside the quote itself rather than only in notes. (8) PAGE IDENTITY HELD, RE-CHECKED. Not one emitted record is a connected-list-DEFINITION control. e0c5f415 splits the work by tool in its own words - 'List Management: The connected list is configured using an expense type as the first field, with an Item Code that ...' versus 'Forms and Fields: The connected list created in List Management is chosen when defining the connected list' - and 39dd2408 places the Connected Lists tab on the Forms and Fields page. Nothing was re-homed here from page.forms-and-fields and nothing here belongs there. I checked the live graph (337 configFields): the ONLY name collision is field.exceptions.newButton, which is benign (ids are namespaced by page) and which I avoided anyway by keeping newListButton. RESIDUAL CONTRADICTION RECORDED, NOT RECONCILED: use-a-connected-list-1eaafd29.md attributes definition work to a third, differently-named 'Connected List Definition tool' under the Shared Configuration administrator, which conflicts with 39dd2408 placing it on the Forms and Fields Connected Lists tab. No field was moved on the strength of either. (9) TWO CONTROLS FLAGGED BUT NOT ADDED. The category-level Save inside Add New List Category is a real, unmodelled third Save - reported in splitsProposed, not emitted, because records created during Repair never face the adversarial refuter. 'Expense Type List Item Key' (e0c5f415, with hard constraints that it must be first in the connected list and is usable in only one definition) is almost certainly a connected-list DEFINITION field belonging to page.forms-and-fields; it is deliberately NOT homed here. (10) MUST-READ FILES: refuter-2 opened all 12; refuter-1 opened the 4 cited by candidates plus 4 more. For my own pass I re-read the two files that actually ground this roster in full - tools-guides/step-1-create-the-source-list-in-list-management-cc91aa73.md and admin-guides/use-a-custom-list-f3fc8bee.md - and confirmed the step sequence, the Note about the EAST; NORTH code format, and the 'make note of the category name and the list name' caveat. I did not re-open overview-8b2edfd0.md, step-2-...-bcaf1f5a.md, overview-of-steps-37e3c289.md, required-roles-53a9a79c.md, field-configuration-information-5813462a.md, additional-documentation-a105a5d7.md, access-connected-lists-39dd2408.md, 76d94b3b.md or e0c5f415.md at this stage: no repair I performed touches them, both refuters read them and reported consistently, and my lens here is assembly of already-refuted records rather than fresh extraction. See mustReadSkipped equivalent in this note. (11) COVERAGE = THIN, AND IT STAYS THIN. All three extraction lenses independently returned coverageVerdict 'thin' and both refuters affirmed it. The reason is not a failed search: grep -rl 'List Management' over BOTH guide directories returns exactly 20 files, 18 of which the extractions read and the remaining 2 (creating-and-approving-a-new-vendor-fa0ecc4e.md, vendor-manager-terminology-8b54bff7.md) yield no controls. There is NO field table, NO option catalog and NO raw <table> for this page anywhere in the corpus. use-a-custom-list-f3fc8bee.md step 5 concedes the gap in the product's own documentation - 'Fill out the remaining options, then select Save.' - and nine topics defer the substance to an external 'Shared: List Management Setup Guide' (called 'Concur Invoice: List Management Setup Guide' in tools-guides/step-4-add-the-custom-field-to-the-employee-form-da376eef.md) that is not in this corpus. The 14 controls here are a procedural skeleton: the nav link, the two New buttons, List Name, the category choice, the item fields, and the three terminal buttons. NOTHING WAS PADDED TO FILL THE GAP, and the automation must be told that the New List page has unnamed options it will encounter and cannot plan for. (12) NAV TRAP RESTATED SO IT IS NOT RE-INTRODUCED: the 'Administration > Invoice' step of each procedure uses non-breaking spaces or an escaped angle bracket ('Click Administration<U+00A0><U+00A0>Invoice.', 'Select Administration\\>Invoice.') and is NOT safely grep -F quotable.
